prompt: Kílódé tí ọmọdé fi nílò ẹ̀kọ́?
prompt_gloss: Why do children need education?
reference: Ọmọdé nílò ẹ̀kọ́ nítorí ọ̀pọ̀ ìdí. Àkọ́kọ́, ẹ̀kọ́ ń kọ́ ọmọdé bí a ṣe ń kà, ń kọ, àti ń ṣe ìṣirò. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, ẹ̀kọ́ ń ràn ọmọdé lọ́wọ́ láti rí iṣẹ́ rere ní ọjọ́ iwájú. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kẹta, ẹ̀kọ́ ń kọ́ ọmọdé nípa àwùjọ, ìwà rere àti bí a ṣe ń gbé pẹ̀lú ẹlòmíràn.
reference_gloss: Children need education for many reasons. First, education teaches a child to read, write and count. Second, education helps a child to find good work in the future. Third, education teaches a child about society, good behaviour and how to live with others.

prompt: Báwo ni a ṣe ń ṣe àmàlà? Ṣe àlàyé ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: How is amala made? Explain in steps.
reference: A ń ṣe àmàlà ní ìgbésẹ̀ wọ̀nyí. Àkọ́kọ́, a ń mú ẹ̀lùbọ́ (ìyẹ̀fun iṣu tàbí ẹ̀gẹ́) wá. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, a ń sè omi títí tí ó fi gbóná. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kẹta, a ń da ẹ̀lùbọ́ náà sínú omi gbígbóná náà, a sì ń yí i títí tí ó fi di ìyẹ̀fun líle tí ó dára.
reference_gloss: Amala is made in these steps. First, you take elubo (yam or cassava flour). Second, you boil water until it is hot. Third, you pour the elubo into the hot water and stir it until it becomes firm, smooth dough.

prompt: Kílódé tí ọjọ́ fi ń lọ, tí òru sì ń bọ̀?
prompt_gloss: Why does the day go and the night come?
reference: Ọjọ́ ń lọ, òru sì ń bọ̀ nítorí pé ilẹ̀ ń yípo ara rẹ̀. Àkọ́kọ́, ilẹ̀ ń yípo ara rẹ̀ ní wákàtí mẹ́rìnlélógún. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, apá ilẹ̀ tí ó dojúkọ oòrùn ni ó ní ọjọ́. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kẹta, nígbà tí apá náà bá yí kúrò lọ́dọ̀ oòrùn, òru ni ó bọ̀.
reference_gloss: Day goes and night comes because the Earth turns on its own axis. First, the Earth turns on its axis once in twenty-four hours. Second, the part of the Earth facing the sun has day. Third, when that part turns away from the sun, night comes.

prompt: Ṣe àlàyé bí a ṣe ń ṣe ọbẹ̀ ẹ̀gúsí.
prompt_gloss: Explain how egusi soup is made.
reference: A ń ṣe ọbẹ̀ ẹ̀gúsí ní ìgbésẹ̀ wọ̀nyí. Àkọ́kọ́, a ń lọ ẹ̀gúsí (ẹ̀so ẹ̀gúsí) títí tí ó fi di ìyẹ̀fun. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, a ń sè ẹ̀gúsí náà pẹ̀lú omi àti epo pupa. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kẹta, a ń fi ẹran, ẹja àti ewé (bíi ugwu) kún un, a sì ń jẹ́ kí ó sè dáadáa kí a tó jẹun.
reference_gloss: Egusi soup is made in these steps. First, you grind egusi (melon seeds) until it becomes a powder. Second, you cook the egusi with water and palm oil. Third, you add meat, fish and vegetables (such as ugwu), and let it cook well before eating.

prompt: Kílódé tí a fi ń wẹ̀ ọwọ́ kí a tó jẹun?
prompt_gloss: Why do we wash our hands before eating?
reference: A ń wẹ̀ ọwọ́ kí a tó jẹun nítorí pé ọwọ́ ń kó àwọn kòkòrò tí a kò lè rí wá. Àkọ́kọ́, kòkòrò wọ̀nyí lè wà lórí ọwọ́ lẹ́yìn tí a bá ti fi ọwọ́ kan onírúurú nǹkan. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, tí a bá jẹun pẹ̀lú ọwọ́ tí kò mọ́, kòkòrò náà lè wọ inú ara, ó sì lè fa àìsàn. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kẹta, wíwẹ̀ ọwọ́ pẹ̀lú omi àti ọṣẹ ń pa kòkòrò náà run.
reference_gloss: We wash our hands before eating because hands carry invisible germs. First, these germs can be on the hands after touching many things. Second, if we eat with dirty hands, the germs can enter the body and cause illness. Third, washing hands with water and soap kills the germs.

prompt: Báwo ni ẹyin ṣe ń di adìyẹ? Ṣe àlàyé ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: How does an egg become a chicken? Explain in steps.
reference: Ẹyin ń di adìyẹ ní ìgbésẹ̀ wọ̀nyí. Àkọ́kọ́, adìyẹ abo ń pọ̀ ẹyin náà, ó sì ń jẹ́ kí ó gbóná fún ọjọ́ mọ́kànlélógún. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, inú ẹyin náà, ọmọ adìyẹ ń dàgbà, ó ń ní ìyẹ́, ẹsẹ̀ àti ẹnu. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kẹta, nígbà tí ó bá dàgbà tó, ó ń fọ́ ìkarahun ẹyin náà, ó sì jáde gẹ́gẹ́ bí ọmọ adìyẹ.
reference_gloss: An egg becomes a chicken in these steps. First, the hen sits on the egg and keeps it warm for twenty-one days. Second, inside the egg, the chick grows, developing feathers, legs and a beak. Third, when it has grown enough, it breaks the shell and comes out as a chick.

prompt: Kílódé tí ìlera fi ṣe pàtàkì?
prompt_gloss: Why is health important?
reference: Ìlera ṣe pàtàkì nítorí ọ̀pọ̀ ìdí. Àkọ́kọ́, ẹni tí ó ní ìlera rere lè ṣiṣẹ́, lè kẹ́kọ̀ọ́, àti lè gbádùn ìgbésí ayé. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, ìlera rere ń dín owó ìtọ́jú ìlera kù, nítorí ẹni tí ó ní ìlera kì í ṣàìsàn nígbà gbogbo. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kẹta, ìlera rere ń ràn ẹni lọ́wọ́ láti pẹ́ ní ayé, àti láti ṣe àwọn ohun tí ó fẹ́.
reference_gloss: Health is important for many reasons. First, a healthy person can work, study and enjoy life. Second, good health reduces the cost of medical care, because a healthy person is not often ill. Third, good health helps a person to live long and to do the things they want.

prompt: Ṣe àlàyé ìdí tí ọkọ̀ ojú omi fi ń léfò lórí omi.
prompt_gloss: Explain why a ship floats on water.
reference: Ọkọ̀ ojú omi ń léfò lórí omi nítorí ìgbésẹ̀ ìṣẹ̀dá kan. Àkọ́kọ́, ọkọ̀ ojú omi ń yí omi kan padà sí ẹ̀gbẹ́, omi náà sì ń tì í sókè. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, agbára ìtìsókè yìí tóbi tó agbára ìwúwo ọkọ̀ náà, nítorí náà ọkọ̀ náà kò lè rì sínú omi. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kẹta, bí ọkọ̀ náà bá wúwo jù, tàbí tí omi bá wọ inú rẹ̀, ó lè rì.
reference_gloss: A ship floats on water because of a law of nature. First, the ship pushes some water aside, and the water pushes it back up. Second, this upward push is as strong as the weight of the ship, so the ship cannot sink. Third, if the ship becomes too heavy, or water enters it, it can sink.

prompt: Adé ń lọ sí ilé ìwé, ó sì rí àgbàlagbà kan tí ó mọ̀ ní ojú ọ̀nà. Àgbàlagbà náà ń dúró, ó ń wo Adé. Kí ni ó yẹ kí Adé ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: Ade is walking to school and sees an elder he knows standing by the roadside. The elder is looking at Ade. What should Ade do? Explain the reason in steps.
reference: Ó yẹ kí Adé dúró kí ó kí àgbàlagbà náà ní ọ̀nà ọ̀wọ̀. Àkọ́kọ́, ìkíni ọ̀wọ̀ ni ọ̀nà tí a fi ń fi ọ̀wọ̀ hàn fún àgbàlagbà ní àṣà Yorùbá. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, bí a bá kọjá àgbàlagbà láìkí i, ó lè rí i gẹ́gẹ́ bí àìbọ̀wọ̀, nítorí náà Adé gbọ́dọ̀ kí i kí ó tó tẹ̀síwájú.
reference_gloss: Ade should stop and greet the elder respectfully. First, a respectful greeting is how Yoruba culture shows honour to an elder. Second, if Ade passes the elder without greeting, the elder may see it as disrespect, so Ade must greet him before walking on.

prompt: Àgbàlagbà kan rán Bọ́lá lọ sí ọjà láti ra ata, ṣùgbọ́n Bọ́lá ń ṣeré bọ́ọ̀lù pẹ̀lú àwọn ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ̀, ó sì kò fẹ́ lọ. Kí ni ó yẹ kí Bọ́lá ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: An elder sends Bola to the market to buy pepper, but Bola is playing football with his friends and does not want to go. What should Bola do? Explain the reason in steps.
reference: Ó yẹ kí Bọ́lá lọ sí ọjà lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀, kí ó sì padà wá tẹ̀síwájú eré náà lẹ́yìn náà. Àkọ́kọ́, ní àṣà Yorùbá, ìbéèrè àgbàlagbà ni a gbọ́dọ̀ tẹ̀lé, nítorí pé àgbàlagbà mọ̀ ju ọmọ lọ. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, ọmọ tí ó ń ṣe ìrànlọ́wọ́ fún àgbàlagbà ń kọ́ ìwà ọmọlúàbí, àgbàlagbà náà sì ń gbẹ́kẹ̀lé e, nítorí náà eré náà lè dúró, ṣùgbọ́n ìbéèrè àgbàlagbà kò gbọ́dọ̀ dúró.
reference_gloss: Bola should go to the market at once and return to the game afterwards. First, in Yoruba culture, an elder's request must be obeyed, because an elder knows more than a child. Second, a child who helps an elder learns good character and the elder trusts him, so the game can wait, but the elder's request must not wait.

prompt: Àlejò kan dé ilé Táyọ̀ ní àkókò oúnjẹ, ó sì jẹ́ ẹni tí Táyọ̀ kò mọ̀ dáadáa. Oúnjẹ tí ó wà nínú ilé kò pọ̀. Kí ni ó yẹ kí Táyọ̀ ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: A guest arrives at Tayo's house at mealtime, and it is someone Tayo does not know well. There is not much food in the house. What should Tayo do? Explain the reason in steps.
reference: Ó yẹ kí Táyọ̀ pè àlejò náà wọlé, kí ó sì fún un ní oúnjẹ àti omi. Àkọ́kọ́, ní àṣà Yorùbá, àlejò ni ẹni tí a gbọ́dọ̀ tọ́jú dáadáa, kódà bí a kò bá mọ̀ ọ́n dáadáa. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, bí a bá fún àlejò ní oúnjẹ, ó ń fi ìfẹ́ àti ọ̀wọ̀ hàn, nítorí náà Táyọ̀ gbọ́dọ̀ pín oúnjẹ tí ó wà fún àlejò náà.
reference_gloss: Tayo should invite the guest in and give him food and water. First, in Yoruba culture, a guest is someone who must be looked after well, even if you do not know him well. Second, giving a guest food shows love and respect, so Tayo must share the food that is there with the guest.

prompt: Àwọn ọmọ márùn-ún ń jẹun papọ̀ láti inú àwo kan, Fúnkẹ́ sì rí pé ẹ̀yà ẹran kan tóbi jùlọ wà nínú àwo náà. Fúnkẹ́ fẹ́ mú ẹ̀yà tóbi náà. Kí ni ó yẹ kí Fúnkẹ́ ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: Five children are eating together from one bowl, and Funke sees that one piece of meat in the bowl is the biggest. Funke wants to take the biggest piece. What should Funke do? Explain the reason in steps.
reference: Ó yẹ kí Fúnkẹ́ mú ẹ̀yà kékeré, kí ó sì fi ẹ̀yà tóbi náà sílẹ̀ fún ẹlòmíràn. Àkọ́kọ́, ní àṣà Yorùbá, ọmọlúàbí kì í gba ohun tóbi jùlọ fún ara rẹ̀ nígbà tí àwọn ẹlòmíràn bá wà. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, bí gbogbo ọmọ bá mú ẹ̀yà tóbi, oúnjẹ kò ní tó fún gbogbo wọn, nítorí náà Fúnkẹ́ gbọ́dọ̀ fi ìwọ̀nba hàn.
reference_gloss: Funke should take a small piece and leave the biggest piece for someone else. First, in Yoruba culture, a well-brought-up child does not take the biggest thing for herself when others are present. Second, if every child takes the biggest piece, the food will not be enough for everyone, so Funke must show moderation.

prompt: Àgbàlagbà kan ń sọ̀rọ̀ ní ìpàdé ìdílé, Ìbùkún sì rí pé àgbàlagbà náà ṣe àṣìṣe ní ohun tí ó ń sọ. Ìbùkún fẹ́ dá a dúró kí ó sì tọ́ ọ. Kí ni ó yẹ kí Ìbùkún ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: An elder is speaking at a family meeting, and Ibukun notices that the elder has made a mistake in what he is saying. Ibukun wants to interrupt him and correct him. What should Ibukun do? Explain the reason in steps.
reference: Ó yẹ kí Ìbùkún dúró, kí ó gbọ́ àgbàlagbà náà tán, kí ó sì sọ èrò rẹ̀ ní ọ̀nà ọ̀wọ̀ lẹ́yìn náà. Àkọ́kọ́, dídá àgbàlagbà dúró nígbà tí ó ń sọ̀rọ̀ jẹ́ àìbọ̀wọ̀ ní àṣà Yorùbá. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, ọmọ lè tọ́ àgbàlagbà ní ọ̀nà ọ̀wọ̀ lẹ́yìn tí ó bá ti parí ọ̀rọ̀ rẹ̀, nítorí náà Ìbùkún gbọ́dọ̀ dúró kí ó sì sọ èrò rẹ̀ lẹ́yìn náà.
reference_gloss: Ibukun should wait, listen to the elder finish, and then share her view respectfully afterwards. First, interrupting an elder while he is speaking is disrespectful in Yoruba culture. Second, a child can correct an elder respectfully after he has finished speaking, so Ibukun must wait and speak afterwards.

prompt: Dáda yá owó mẹ́wàá ẹgbẹ̀rún naira lọ́wọ́ ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ̀, ó sì ṣèlérí pé yóò san án padà ní ọjọ́ Jímọ̀. Ọjọ́ Jímọ̀ dé, Dáda kò ní owó náà. Kí ni ó yẹ kí Dáda ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: Dada borrowed ten thousand naira from his friend and promised to pay it back on Friday. Friday arrives and Dada does not have the money. What should Dada do? Explain the reason in steps.
reference: Ó yẹ kí Dáda lọ sọ́dọ̀ ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ̀ kí ó tó di ọjọ́ Jímọ̀, kí ó sọ ìdí tí kò fi ní owó náà, kí ó sì béèrè fún ọjọ́ míràn. Àkọ́kọ́, ẹni tí ó yá owó gbọ́dọ̀ pa ìlérí rẹ̀ mọ́, nítorí pé ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé ni ìpìlẹ̀ ọ̀rẹ́. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, bí Dáda bá sọ òtítọ́ kí ó tó di ọjọ́ tí a yàn, ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ̀ lè gbà á, nítorí náà Dáda kò gbọ́dọ̀ fi pamọ́ títí di ọjọ́ Jímọ̀.
reference_gloss: Dada should go to his friend before Friday, explain why he does not have the money, and ask for another day. First, a person who borrows money must keep his promise, because trust is the foundation of friendship. Second, if Dada tells the truth before the agreed day, his friend may accept it, so Dada must not hide it until Friday.

prompt: Alábàágbà kan rí ọmọ alábàágbà míràn tí ó ń ṣe ohun búburú ní òpópónà, ó ń fi òkúta lù àwọn ọmọdé kékeré. Òbí ọmọ náà kò sí níbẹ̀. Kí ni ó yẹ kí alábàágbà náà ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: A neighbour sees another neighbour's child doing something bad in the street, throwing stones at small children. The child's parent is not there. What should the neighbour do? Explain the reason in steps.
reference: Ó yẹ kí alábàágbà náà dá ọmọ náà dúró ní ọ̀nà tútù, kí ó sì sọ fún òbí rẹ̀ lẹ́yìn náà. Àkọ́kọ́, ní àṣà Yorùbá, gbogbo àgbàlagbà ni òbí gbogbo ọmọ, nítorí náà alábàágbà lè tọ́ ọmọ náà. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, ìbáwí tútù ni a gbọ́dọ̀ lò, kì í ṣe ìkọlù, nítorí pé ọmọ náà kì í ṣe ọmọ alábàágbà náà, nítorí náà ó gbọ́dọ̀ dá a dúró tútù kí ó sì sọ fún òbí rẹ̀.
reference_gloss: The neighbour should stop the child gently and tell the parent afterwards. First, in Yoruba culture, every elder is a parent to every child, so the neighbour may correct the child. Second, gentle correction must be used, not harsh punishment, because the child is not the neighbour's own child, so he must stop the child gently and tell the parent.

prompt: Ìdílé kan ní ìsìnkú, àwọn alábàágbà sì béèrè fún owó ìrànlọ́wọ́ láti ọ̀dọ̀ gbogbo ẹbí àti alábàágbà. Ọ̀kan lára àwọn ọmọ ìdílé náà ní owó díẹ̀, ó sì ń ronú pé òun kò ní san án. Kí ni ó yẹ kí ọmọ náà ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: A family is holding a funeral, and the elders ask every family member and neighbour for a contribution. One member of the family has little money and is thinking of paying nothing. What should that person do? Explain the reason in steps.
reference: Ó yẹ kí ọmọ náà san ohun tí ó lè san, kódà bí ó bá kéré. Àkọ́kọ́, ìrànlọ́wọ́ ní àkókò ìṣòro ni ọ̀nà tí ìdílé fi ń fi ìfẹ́ hàn, kì í ṣe iye owó náà ni ó ṣe pàtàkì jùlọ. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, bí gbogbo ẹni bá san díẹ̀, owó náà yóò tó, nítorí náà ọmọ náà gbọ́dọ̀ san ohun tí ó lè san, kì í ṣe kí ó kọ̀ láti san rárá.
reference_gloss: That person should pay what he can, even if it is small. First, helping in a time of trouble is how a family shows love, and it is not the amount of money that matters most. Second, if everyone pays a little, the money will be enough, so the person must pay what he can, not refuse to pay at all.

prompt: Àgbàlagbà kan wọ inú bọ́ọ̀sì, ó sì ń dúró, nítorí pé gbogbo ìjókòó ti kún. Ọmọdé kan jókòó níbẹ̀, ó ń wo fóònù rẹ̀. Kí ni ó yẹ kí ọmọdé náà ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: An elder boards a bus and is standing, because every seat is taken. A young person is sitting there, looking at his phone. What should the young person do? Explain the reason in steps.
reference: Ó yẹ kí ọmọdé náà dìde kí ó fún àgbàlagbà náà ní ìjókòó rẹ̀. Àkọ́kọ́, ní àṣà Yorùbá, ọmọ gbọ́dọ̀ fi ìjókòó rẹ̀ fún àgbàlagbà, nítorí pé àgbàlagbà yẹ fún ọ̀wọ̀. Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì, àgbàlagbà lè rẹ̀wẹ̀sì ní kíákíá ju ọmọ lọ, nítorí náà ọmọdé náà gbọ́dọ̀ dìde kí ó sì fún un ní ìjókòó náà.
reference_gloss: The young person should stand up and give the elder his seat. First, in Yoruba culture, a young person must give his seat to an elder, because an elder deserves respect. Second, an elder can get tired more quickly than a young person, so the young person must stand up and give him the seat.

prompt: Adé gbọ́ ọ̀rọ̀ kan nípa ọmọ alábàágbà rẹ̀, pé ọmọ náà kùnà nínú ìdánwò ilé ìwé, àwọn òbí rẹ̀ sì ń fi í pamọ́. Adé kò mọ̀ bóyá ọ̀rọ̀ náà jẹ́ òtítọ́ tàbí èké. Àwọn ọ̀rẹ́ Adé fẹ́ kí ó sọ ọ̀rọ̀ náà fún gbogbo ènìyàn. Kí ni ó yẹ kí Adé ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
prompt_gloss: Ade hears a rumour about his neighbour's child, that the child failed his school exams and his parents are hiding it. Ade does not know whether the rumour is true or false. Ade's friends want him to tell everyone the rumour. What should Ade do? Explain the reason in steps.

prompt: Ẹbí kan ń jà nípa ilẹ̀ ìdílé, ẹ̀gbọ́n àti àbúrò ń bá ara wọn wí. Ẹ̀gbọ́n fẹ́ lọ sí ilé ẹjọ́ lẹ́sẹ̀kẹsẹ̀. Kí ni ó yẹ kí ẹbí náà ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.

reference_gloss: The family should let the family elders settle it first, listening to both the elder brother and the younger brother. prompt: Ọmọdé kan ń pè àgbàlagbà kan ní orúkọ rẹ̀, ó ń sọ pé, 'Báyọ̀, wá nihin.' Àgbàlagbà náà ju ọmọdé náà lọ ní ọjọ́ orí gidigidi. Kí ni ó yẹ kí ọmọdé náà ṣe? Ṣe àlàyé ìdí rẹ̀ ní ìgbésẹ̀.
